title: Use Case Optimal Queries Returning Unstructured Tuples
pattern: Bypassing domain models to fetch custom display datasets, but returning raw, un-named tuples (e.g., `(String, i64, f64)`) directly to higher layers.
why_bad: It is highly fragile. Any change in SQL projection column ordering causes compile-time mismatches or silent runtime semantic bugs (e.g., swapping count and balance).
detection: Database querying functions returning raw generic tuples containing 3 or more primitive fields.
counterexample: Two-element helper tuples (such as key-value pairs `(u64, String)`) in local collections. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix:
Define a structured, named value object or struct specifically representing the optimal query result layout.
```rust
struct UserDashboardView {
    name: String,
    orders_count: i64,
    balance: f64,
}
```
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 12, p. 228, 517).
